newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says no salmon deal with Canada.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says no salmon deal with Canada.

text.p: The United States said Thursday that it had failed to resolve a Pacific salmon dispute with Canada before the start of the 1997 fishing season.

"In the absence of agreement this summer, U.S. managers will ensure that our 1997 fisheries are conducted in accordance with sound conservation and management principles and will coordinate with Canadian managers to that end," the State Department said.
During the failed talks, the United States put forward a package of proposals that would involve "major financial and social costs to U.S. interests," a statement said.

It said the proposals included a regime to rebuild depleted coho salmon stocks and a "significant" restructuring of the U.S. fishing fleet to reduce its catch of the so-called Fraser River sockeye. In addition, the United States discussed establishment of a fund to conserve salmon stocks off the West Coast.

"Canada, however, was unwilling to make or accept a proposal that would meet the minimum necessary to assure conservation of Canadian and U.S. wild coho stocks, let alone allow both countries to maintain viable coho fisheries," the State Department said.

"In the end, Canada wanted the United States to make a substantial reduction in its sockeye fishery in return for a coho regime that would not ensure cnservation and would not provide a coho fishery for the United States," it added.
